clues.text: When Mordecai would not bow down to him at the king's gate in Susa, he was filled with rage.
King Xerxes removed the signet ring from his finger and gave it to him, the enemy of the Jews.
In the days of King Xerxes, the Pur, that is the lot, was cast before him to choose a day and month.
His wife Zeresh and his friends told him to build a gallows fifty cubits high for Mordecai.
Thinking King Xerxes wanted to honor him, he had to robe Mordecai and parade him on the king's horse.
King Xerxes told Queen Esther that the Jews in the citadel of Susa had killed five hundred men, including his ten sons.
In Susa, he was hanged on the gallows he had prepared for Mordecai, and the king's fury subsided.
